correctness.rationale: Inclusion-exclusion over all 128 absent-point subsets yields explicit Fano and full-model survival laws for every integer t>=1. The seven Fano lines and 35 unrestricted triples give the stated signed avoidance counts. The difference equals (21*5^t-35*4^t+35)/35^t and has zero values t=1,2. Writing a_t=(4^t-1)/5^t gives a_1=a_2=3/5 and a_t-a_(t+1)=(4^t-4)/5^(t+1)>0 for t>=2, proving positivity for every t>=3; t=0 has equal tails. The local standalone exact Fraction checker verifies 128 subset counts against independent forward Markov DP for t=0..12, exact t=3 difference 12/1225 and mean gap 7/527. No infinite proof is inferred from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The all-integer strict first-order stochastic ordering is not implied by an expectation inequality alone. The directly relevant source arXiv:2606.28216v1 (Theorem 2.1 and Section 3) proves the two means, and its Fano Markov-stage data are not an all-time comparison against the full 35-triple law. The new result derives both exact distributional formulas and proves positivity at every horizon through an avoidance-factor cancellation and monotone ratio. Further primary studies are expectation-focused and no semantically searched record was found covering this all-time claim; coverage risks remain and this is not an absolute novelty certificate.
residual_risks: An earlier result absent from indexed records or not found under the tested equivalent terms could state or imply the same inequality.
The Fano stages in the 2026 paper contain enough data to derive its marginal law; a previously unrecognized published full-model comparison could imply the tail ordering.
No claim is made for larger projective planes or for arbitrary fair mechanisms.

value.rationale: This canonical seven-line design is the first explicitly proved expectation-level fair-covering counterexample. The new theorem strengthens the claim structurally to all stopping-time quantiles and all increasing costs (when integrable), revealing a uniform-in-time coverage-delay mechanism rather than a small aggregate mean difference. The exact formula makes the effect attributable to triple-avoidance counts even though one-point and pair structure agree. A full stochastic-order resolution for the natural first example is a motivated precise invariant and useful boundary case independent of any larger-plane classification. The previously known means are credited, and larger-design significance is not claimed.
